factProposals.value: Across all 274 real hospitals in production (OK+TX rural/Critical Access), 257 are flagged by at least one early-warning criterion, 16 cannot be fully assessed (missing current-year metrics or fewer than 3 years of data), and 1 is genuinely healthy on all three criteria.
factProposals.evidence: pipeline/early_warning.py (run() output against production Supabase, spot-checked per-hospital)

factProposals.value: "Days in A/R rising two years in a row" cannot be honestly evaluated when a hospital has a reporting gap (a missing fiscal year already known to exist in this dataset) between its available years, since the three years being compared would not actually be consecutive.

decisions.statement: A criterion whose required metric is missing is reported as 'not_assessable', never as 'not_triggered', and a hospital is only 'not_flagged' overall if every one of its three criteria was actually checked.
decisions.rationale: An early-warning system that quietly clears a hospital it couldn't actually check would defeat its own purpose -- treating missing data as 'no problem found' is a false negative, not a neutral outcome.

decisions.statement: Overall hospital status uses the precedence flagged > not_assessable > not_flagged, so a real trigger on one criterion is never hidden by an unrelated missing metric on another.
decisions.rationale: The point of the system is to surface real problems; a missing operating-margin figure must not suppress a genuine days-cash-on-hand trigger found elsewhere.

decisions.statement: Flags are stored as one current-state row per hospital (early_warning_flags, primary key provider_ccn), replaced via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on every run, not appended as a history log.
decisions.rationale: Matches the project-wide idempotency requirement -- re-running the evaluator after a new fiscal year is imported must update a hospital's flag state, not accumulate duplicate or stale rows.
decisions.evidence: pipeline/schema.sql (early_warning_flags table + verified live: 274 rows before and after a second run, identical distribution)

decisions.statement: The flag evaluator queries the latest 3 fiscal years per hospital using the same 'partition by hospital, order by fiscal_year desc, limit 3' shape as the public Health Snapshot's own trend query.
decisions.rationale: So the flag evaluator and the public-facing trend page can never disagree about which years count as 'the latest three' for the same hospital.

decisions.statement: The new early_warning_flags table has the same public-read RLS policy as hospitals and cost_report_years.
decisions.rationale: This data is derived entirely from public CMS cost reports with no management-company-specific scoping yet -- STORY-006 (row-level security) and STORY-005 (operator uploads, the thing that would actually need company-level scoping) are not built yet.

limitations.statement: The evaluator recomputes flags for every hospital on each run rather than only hospitals whose metrics changed since the last run -- fine at 274 rows, would need a changed-since filter at meaningfully larger scale.
Flag history is not retained -- each run overwrites the previous evaluation for a hospital, so there is no way yet to see when a hospital's status changed over time.
limitations.evidence: pipeline/schema.sql (early_warning_flags primary key is provider_ccn alone)
